candidates.title: Support streamlined login methods
candidates.statement: The system shall support streamlined staff login methods (for example, card-swipe) as an available login option.
candidates.source_quote: We've seen other library systems implement card-swipe login for their ILS terminals.
candidates.priority_signals: Raised as a front-line improvement; included in Katherine's summary to add to requirements list.

candidates.title: Support username/password login
candidates.statement: The system shall support traditional individual username and password login as a login method.
candidates.source_quote: we also need to support the traditional username/password method - not all staff may have ID cards
candidates.priority_signals: Called out as necessary fallback; included in Katherine's summary.

candidates.title: Streamlined login optional
candidates.statement: The system shall make streamlined staff login methods optional and shall not require use of streamlined methods.
candidates.source_quote: The streamlined method should be optional but available.
candidates.priority_signals: Susan: "the system should not REQUIRE the streamlined login"; Katherine included 'supports (but does not require)'.

candidates.title: Do not require card-reader hardware
candidates.statement: The system shall operate without requiring card-reader hardware so branches without card-reader infrastructure can use the system.
candidates.source_quote: Some of our smaller branches may not have the infrastructure for card readers.
candidates.priority_signals: Explicit concern about smaller branches lacking infrastructure; stated as a requirement not to require streamlined login.

candidates.title: Card-swipe must identify individual
candidates.statement: The system shall ensure that any card-swipe streamlined login method identifies the individual staff member and shall not bypass individual authentication.
candidates.source_quote: the system must track WHICH staff member is logged in for audit purposes...it shouldn't bypass individual authentication entirely.

candidates.title: Immediate streamlined login
candidates.statement: The system shall allow streamlined login methods (e.g., card-swipe) to log a staff member in immediately upon successful use.
candidates.source_quote: The staff member simply swipes their employee ID badge and is logged in immediately.
candidates.priority_signals: Described as much faster in practice; front-line time saving rationale.

candidates.title: Streamlined login improves security
candidates.statement: The system shall provide streamlined login options that reduce security risks associated with password sharing and terminals left logged in compared with manual login.
candidates.source_quote: This is much faster and more secure.
candidates.priority_signals: Rationale includes preventing password sharing and leaving terminals logged in.

candidates.title: Audit log of staff logins
candidates.statement: The system shall record, for audit purposes, which staff member is logged in when any login occurs.
candidates.source_quote: The system must track WHICH staff member is logged in for audit purposes.
candidates.priority_signals: "this is important"; requested for audit purposes

candidates.title: Permissions determined by role at login
candidates.statement: The system shall determine a staff member's permissions at login according to the staff member's assigned security group or role.
candidates.source_quote: when a staff member logs in (by any method), their permissions should be determined by their assigned security group/role.
candidates.priority_signals: Raised as requirement linking login to permissions; included in discussion of role-based access.

candidates.title: User rights via security groups/roles
candidates.statement: The system shall control user rights and privileges through configurable security groups and/or roles.
candidates.source_quote: User rights and privileges controlled through security groups/roles.
candidates.priority_signals: Listed in Katherine's summary; multiple people requested role-based access.

candidates.title: Administrators manage groups and roles
candidates.statement: The system shall allow administrators to create, modify, and delete security groups and roles and to manage their membership.
candidates.source_quote: Administrators should be able to create and manage these groups.
candidates.stakeholder: Susan Sexton-Cooley; George Tuttle; Katherine Gregory
candidates.priority_signals: Requested by multiple stakeholders; implied in Katherine's 'easy administration' summary.

candidates.title: Easy role administration
candidates.statement: The system shall make administration of roles and permissions easy so that changing someone's permissions is accomplished by changing their role assignment rather than editing individual permissions.
candidates.source_quote: changing someone's permissions should be a simple matter of changing their role assignment, not modifying individual permissions.
candidates.priority_signals: Explicit usability/administration requirement; included in Katherine's summary.

candidates.title: Assign roles to individuals and groups
candidates.statement: The system shall allow assignment of roles and access controls to individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups.
candidates.source_quote: This would allow access control for individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups.
candidates.priority_signals: Listed in Katherine's summary as a key requirement.

candidates.title: Predefined role capability examples
candidates.statement: The system shall support roles that provide distinct example capabilities such as: front desk staff can run basic reports with limited filters; department heads can create and modify templates; system administrators have full access to reports and permissions.
candidates.source_quote: Front desk staff (can run basic reports, limited filters)...Department heads (can create and modify templates)...System administrators (full access)
candidates.priority_signals: Provided as concrete role examples by Piedmont Regional Library.

candidates.title: Automatic session lock or logout
candidates.statement: The system shall provide mechanisms (for example automatic session lock or logout) to prevent terminals being left logged in and to reduce password sharing security risks.
candidates.source_quote: staff get in a hurry and sometimes share passwords or leave terminals logged in.
candidates.priority_signals: Raised as a frontline security problem to be addressed.
